symptom: `describe workflow` of a workflow whose branch ends the workflow (Studio Pro: an End at the end of a user-task outcome) printed `'Reject' { }`. Re-executed, the branch fell through into the main flow — every later task was created for a request already rejected — with check, exec and mx check all clean. MDL also had no statement to write such an End, so authored workflows had the same fallthrough.
cause: formatWorkflowActivities skipped every EndWorkflowActivity as 'implicit', but only the main flow's End is implicit; the function is shared by the top level and every nested flow. On the write side, the first workflow grammar dropped `workflowEndStmt` for colliding with the closing END WORKFLOW, leaving ast.WorkflowEndNode and buildEndWorkflow unwired.
fix: Top-level body split into workflowMainBody (no End statement) and workflowBody for brace blocks (accepts `end workflow [comment '...']`, walked in child order); describer skips only the main flow's End; builder reserves the implicit Start/End names; MDL-WF08..11 (validate_workflow_end.go) predict CE1844/CE6671/CE6689/`return`; checkNoDroppedWorkflowConstructs refuses a rewrite that deletes stored nested Ends. An End's Name is a fixed base 'End' (de-duplicated), never its caption.
insight: A shared formatter with a skip meant for one call site is a silent data-loss bug on every other call site — and the output still parsed, so round-trip tests that only re-parse cannot see it; the defect is semantic (fallthrough), visible only in the rebuilt graph or at runtime. Three measurement lessons: (1) a spike that swaps a placeholder `call microflow END_<caption>` for an AST node measured every placement before any grammar existed, with the caption doubling as attribution in mxbuild's messages; (2) the reachability rule needed rows a reading of CE6689 would not suggest — jumps terminate a path as surely as an End, termination reaches through a nested decision, and a main flow ending in a direct jump is CE6679 as well; (3) a test fixture called 'a valid workflow' (a main flow ending in `jump to`) was the second time a new rule proved that fixture invalid — measure the fixture, not the rule, before weakening either. (4) Deriving an activity Name from its caption, the pattern every other builder uses, was wrong for an End: `end workflow comment 'Rejected by manager'` built CE7247 'The name ... is not valid'. The end-to-end fixture passed because every caption in it was one word; the doctype script's spaced caption is what caught it. An End is never referenced by name, so a fixed base name removes the whole class instead of sanitising it — and a fixture's captions should include a space whenever a name may be derived from one.
